answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. To mint identities, each agent broadcasts a cryptographic pulse linking its hardware-rooted cipher signature to locked collateral. Minting fees scale exponentially with cluster size ($O(2^n)$), forcing exponential capital exhaustion for Sybil swarms while leaving honest nodes stable, like bedrock beneath a fragile karst landscape.
